World.title: Fault lines beneath Mulembe's United Opposition
World.content:
Mulembe unity faces fresh cracks as leaders jostle for influence ahead of 2027. [Courtesy, Meta]

For a community that has spent months talking about unity, the events at Gloria Khalwale’s burial in Malinya offered a revealing glimpse of what lies beneath the surface of the Mulembe political family.

The leaders may be walking under the same opposition umbrella, sharing platforms and speaking of a common political future, but yesterday, the smiles briefly gave way to something more difficult to hide: the contest over who should lead, who should follow and, perhaps most importantly, who should have the final word.

World.title: City Hall in rush to expand drainage system ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja during an inspection tour of the ongoing drainage system expansion. [GPS]

Nairobi County has embarked on drainage expansion works aimed at mitigating floodwaters ahead of El Nino rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, while calling on city residents to remain alert and proactive, said City Hall has intensified preparations and accelerated identification of hotspots.

The governor on Friday said his administration is taking early and coordinated action to minimise the impact of heavy rains, urging residents to stay calm, pay attention to official information and follow guidance from the multi-agency team established to coordinate the city’s preparedness and emergency response.

“We are working proactively to address the challenges of flooding before El Nino hits the ground. We urge our people not to panic but to be alert and get information from our multi-agency team,” said Sakaja.

The Governor spoke during an inspection tour of several flood-prone areas in Nairobi, including the Mombasa Road-Bunyala Junction corridor and Globe Roundabout, which experienced significant flooding during previous heavy rains.

Sakaja said drainage works are already underway in the affected areas, with teams working to open up and deepen drainage channels, clear obstructions, and improve storm-water flow to prevent a repeat of the flooding witnessed previously.

His remarks come as weatherman warned of increased rainfall in the coming months, with Nairobi among the urban areas requiring heightened preparedness because of its exposure to flooding and the impact of heavy rainfall on roads, settlements and other critical infrastructure.

Sakaja said the county has so far brought together the disaster management teams, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) under a coordinated programme worth Sh2.4 billion to strengthen Nairobi’s flood resilience.

Of the amount, Sh2 billion has been set aside for drainage and flood-mitigation works targeting 19 roads in flood-prone areas.

The projects are at an advanced stage, with tenders awarded and contractors expected to commence implementation after completion of the necessary processes.

Sakaja reiterated that the programme will complement ongoing county interventions under the Nairobi Regeneration Programme, which includes the rehabilitation and upgrading of critical infrastructure across the city.

“The Sh2 billion will support a comprehensive drainage overhaul that complements the ongoing Nairobi Regeneration Programme. Our goal is to permanently address the flooding challenges that have affected the city for many years,” Sakaja said.

He said the focus is not only on responding to floods after they occur, but on addressing the infrastructure weaknesses that have historically made Nairobi vulnerable to flooding.

To strengthen preparedness, the county has established five specialised sub-committees under the multi-agency framework.

The committees include Infrastructure and Drainage; Emergency Response and Evacuation; Shelter and Relief; Security and Traffic and Communication.

While the Infrastructure and Drainage committee will coordinate the clearing and improvement of drainage systems, rivers and other critical infrastructure, the Emergency Response and Evacuation committee will oversee rapid response, rescue and evacuation operations whenever emergencies occur.

The Shelter and Relief committee will prepare safe shelters and coordinate the provision of food, water, medical assistance and other essential support to affected residents.

The Security and Traffic committee will coordinate security, traffic management and emergency access, while the Communication committee will strengthen early-warning systems, public alerts and timely dissemination of information.

Sakaja said the county is also mobilising personnel, equipment and other resources to clear blocked drains, remove silt and waste and strengthen emergency response systems in areas identified as vulnerable.

He urged residents and their associations, businesses and other stakeholders to play an active role in flood preparedness by keeping drainage areas clear and paying attention to official warnings.

The county chief said residents in high-risk areas will be provided with timely information on emerging weather conditions and the actions they should take when heavy rains occur.

“We don’t want people to panic. We want people to be proactive, to listen to information and to work with us. The multi-agency team is in place, and we are preparing before the rains intensify,” Sakaja said.

According to him, the multi-agency approach will also help eliminate jurisdictional gaps by bringing together national and county agencies to operate as one coordinated team.

He said the combination of drainage upgrades, emergency preparedness, early-warning systems and coordinated response would strengthen Nairobi’s resilience and reduce disruption caused by heavy rains.

The multi-agency team is expected to meet next week to review progress, coordinate ongoing works and further push the city’s El Niño preparedness agenda.

World.title: Public officers eyeing elective posts to resign by February 10 - IEBC
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon addressing the press at a past press conference. [File, Standard]

Public officers seeking to contest elective positions in the 2027 General Election have until February 10, 2027, to resign from office, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has announced.

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon said the deadline falls exactly six months before the August 10, 2027, General Election, which the Commission has confirmed will be held on a Tuesday.

“Any public officer who intends to contest in this election must resign from public office by Wednesday, 10th February 2027, which is exactly six months before the election,” Ethekon said.

The IEBC said adherence to the timelines will be non-negotiable, noting that they are legally binding and essential to ensuring an orderly electoral process.

Under the timetable, political parties must submit their membership lists and details of candidates participating in party primaries by March 16, 2027.

Party primaries and any related disputes must be concluded by May 8, while independent candidates are also required to meet their legal obligations by the same date.

Presidential aspirants will have until May 24 to submit lists of supporting voters drawn from a majority of Kenya’s counties.

Candidate registration will begin on May 29, with specific deadlines applying to the various elective positions.

The official campaign period will commence after candidates are registered, but not earlier than May 29, 2027.

Ethekon warned political parties, candidates and their supporters against breaching the prescribed campaign period, saying any electioneering outside the legal window will be unlawful.

The restrictions cover campaign posters, billboards, political caravans and other forms of campaigning.

Campaigning will close on August 7, 2027, 48 hours before Kenyans head to the polls.

“The law prescribes when election campaigns may commence,” Ethekon said, urging political parties, candidates and their supporters to strictly comply with electoral laws and regulations.

The deadline is among key milestones unveiled by the electoral commission as political parties, aspirants and other stakeholders begin preparations for the next General Election.

World.title: Schools will open on August 24 as scheduled, Ogamba says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Students heading home during recent demonstrations. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Ministry of Education said the official academic calendar remains unchanged.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, August 19, Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba insists that learners will return to school on Monday, August 24, 2026.

The CS has dismissed reports circulating on social media claiming that the reopening of schools for the third term has been postponed, warning parents, teachers, learners and education stakeholders against relying on unauthorised online notices.

“We wish to clarify that the academic calendar for Basic Education institutions and Teacher Training Colleges remains unchanged,” the CS said.

The clarification comes two days before the scheduled reopening of schools, amid reports circulating on social media platforms suggesting that the government had pushed back the start of Term III.

"Our attention has been drawn to misleading information circulating on various social media platforms, purporting that the academic calendar for basic education institutions and Teachers Training Colleges has been changed," he stated.

The Ministry termed the reports “FALSE” and urged members of the public to completely disregard them.

Ogamba said the Ministry had directed Regional Directors of Education, County Directors of Education and Sub-County Directors of Education to ensure strict compliance with the approved academic calendar contained in a circular dated October 9, 2025.

According to the Ministry, pre-primary, primary, junior, senior and secondary schools will begin Term III on Monday, August 24. The term will run for nine weeks and end on October 23, 2026.

The reopening marks the final academic term of the school year, with schools expected to implement the approved programmes as they prepare learners for the end-of-year national assessments and examinations.

Diploma Teachers Training Colleges will also resume academic operations on August 24, with their third term scheduled to conclude on November 6, 2026.

The Ministry further confirmed that the national assessment and examination calendar has not been altered for KPSEA, KILEA, KJSEA, KPLEA and KCSE are scheduled to begin from October 26, 2026, as earlier announced.

The Ministry also reminded schools that extracurricular activities and visits to secondary schools will remain banned during Term III.

The latest clarification is part of efforts by the government to prevent confusion among parents, learners and teachers as schools prepare to reopen.

Ogamba urged education stakeholders to obtain information through official Ministry communication channels, rather than social media posts whose authenticity cannot be established.

“Parents, teachers and learners and members of the public are advised to strictly rely on the Ministry's official communication channels and field officers for accurate information," he said.

World.title: Ruto denies Sh104bn SHA technology contract
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto has dismissed claims that the government entered into a controversial Sh104 billion contract with Safaricom and Apeiro Limited for the Social Health Authority (SHA) technology system.

Speaking on Tuesday evening at the Presidential Townhall held during the National Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto defended the government's investment in digital health, saying the technology was designed to improve transparency and accountability in the management of SHA services.

“There is no Sh104 billion contract. What we have done is design a digital system to make sure that everything is visible. Every treatment must be traceable, and every payment must be accounted for,” Ruto said.

He explained that the government had not purchased the technology outright but had engaged investors who own the equipment, with the State paying for the services provided.

His remarks were echoed by Digital Health Agency Chief Executive Anthony Lenaiyara, who rejected claims that SHA had committed Sh104 billion to technology upgrades.

“It is not correct or true that SHA has undertaken any upgrade or invested Sh104 billion in technology upgrades. What we did is build a digital superhighway comprising 43 systems to support Universal Health Coverage,” Lenaiyara said.

Lenaiyara said the technology infrastructure had been rolled out without requiring health facilities to purchase the devices, adding that the system had transformed the processing and accountability of SHA claims.

He contrasted the new system with the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) model, where claims were processed using physical files that moved between different offices for verification and approval.

Ruto also addressed other government programmes, saying the State had mobilised resources to construct 23,000 additional classrooms to ease pressure caused by shortages of learning spaces.

World.title: 'That was not healthcare, it was theft'- Ruto on old health system
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during the official opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC), Nairobi, August 18,2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has accused the defunct National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) system of enabling theft from sick Kenyans, citing claims for procedures that never happened.

Speaking on Tuesday, August 18, at the opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto described the old system as opaque and vulnerable to abuse.

"We heard of claims for procedures that never happened, fictitious patients and inflated bills. That was not healthcare, it was theft, and theft from sick Kenyans," said Ruto.

He called digital health systems the backbone holding the reforms together and said they would close loopholes that let people profit from the system's weaknesses.

Ruto ranked Universal Health Coverage (UHC) alongside the Affordable Housing Programme as one of the government's most consequential social transformation efforts, crediting collaboration between national and county governments for changes in how healthcare is financed, delivered and accounted for.

The two-day summit, themed "Reforms Delivered, Health as a Right," has drawn more than 5,000 delegates to audit progress under the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) and set priorities for the remainder of Ruto's term, according to Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale.

Ruto said 32.3 million Kenyans are now registered with the Social Health Authority (SHA), which replaced NHIF in October 2024.

Eight million have received treatment, more than 1.2 million mothers have been supported to deliver safely and more than 500,000 surgical procedures have been supported, he added.

He put Kenyans' previous annual out-of-pocket health spending at Sh150 billion ($1.16 billion), saying families had borrowed, sold assets or organised harambees to cover medical costs before the reforms.

"Millions paid out of pocket, borrowed, sold assets, organised harambees or stayed away from hospital because they could not afford care," said Ruto.

Since October 2024, SHA has received more than Sh209 billion ($1.62 billion) and paid more than Sh178 billion ($1.38 billion) to contracted facilities across all 47 counties, Ruto added.

He credited 107,800 Community Health Promoters, deployed under a shared financing arrangement between national and county governments, with reaching more than nine million households and referring over 750,000 people for further treatment.

On supply chains, Ruto said the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority's (KEMSA) fill rate had risen from about 40 per cent to 91 per cent, helped by a Sh1.5 billion ($11.6 million) recapitalisation and a Sh10 billion ($77.4 million) credit line.

The reforms rest on four laws Ruto signed on 19 October 2023: the Primary Health Care Act, the Social Health Insurance Act, the Digital Health Act and the Facilities Improvement Financing Act.

Ruto acknowledged gaps remained in registration, benefit clarity, claims processing and digital systems.

"The ultimate measure of reform is not the laws we pass or the numbers we register, but the experience of the patient in terms of dependable, affordable and dignified care," said Ruto.

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki, Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, Duale and Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja attended the opening session, alongside county governors, principal secretaries, members of Parliament and development partners.

The summit runs through Wednesday.

World.title: Gachagua: Opposition does not need Uhuru's money to send Ruto home
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua during a church service at PCEA Rev. Samuel Marima Memorial Church in Gatundu South, Kiambu on August 16, 2026. [Kimaku Chege, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed claims that former President Uhuru Kenyatta is financing opposition activities against President William Ruto.

Addressing the allegations that Kenyatta was financing opposition campaigns, Gachagua insisted that the movement did not require money from the former President.

Gachagua says the movement seeking political change is driven by Kenyans and does not depend on financial sponsorship.

“Nasikia kwamba Uhuru is sponsoring us to campaign against you. Uhuru is not sponsoring us, we don't need any sponsorship, this is a mass movement for change which does not need funding,” he said.

He was speaking on Sunday, August 16, 2026, during a church service at PCEA Rev. Samuel Marima Memorial Church in Gatundu South, Kiambu County.

Gachagua further said the opposition had sufficient public support to challenge the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election, insisting that Kenyans themselves were the driving force behind calls for a change of government.

He added that the public itself would determine the political fate of the Ruto administration.

“We don't need money but Kenyans will send you home,” Gachagua said.

The comments come against the backdrop of renewed debate over political alliances and the role of former leaders in Kenya's 2027 succession politics. Kenyatta, who served as President from 2013 to 2022, has largely remained outside the day-to-day administration of government since handing over power to Ruto.

Gachagua also defended Kenyatta against what he described as attempts to drag the former President into the current political contest.

“Uhuru Kenyatta asiguzwe na mtu yeyote. Alindwe na atetewe na apatiwe amani. Uhuru alifanya kazi yake na akastaafu,” Gachagua said.

The former Deputy President said Kenyatta should not be treated as a political candidate or blamed for the activities of opposition politicians.

“Nimemwambia Ruto unauliza Uhuru nini na sio candidate in the next election. I am your main opponent,” Gachagua said.

His remarks came amid an increasingly heated political contest over the direction of the country ahead of the 2027 elections.

Ruto and his administration have faced criticism from opposition figures over the economy, cost of living and the government's record since taking office.

Gachagua's comments also followed his broader criticism of the government's economic record.

Earlier in the church address, he challenged Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi's argument that increased consumption of soft drinks could indicate improved household incomes.

Gachagua argued that ordinary Kenyans were experiencing economic difficulties despite government claims of improved economic indicators. He said declining church offerings would provide a more meaningful indication of household financial wellbeing.

“If you want to know if the economy is doing well, ask the pastor about the offering; it will tell you how the economy is moving,” he said.

He further urged Kenyans to prepare for political change in 2027, arguing that the country required new leadership.

“Let us get in line. We look for new leadership that will fix our country and return it to where Uhuru Kenyatta left us,” Gachagua said

World.title: Gachagua: We will protect ourselves against goons
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua addresses residents of Naivasha where he lashed out at President William and told him to keep of former President Uhuru Kenyatta. [Antony Gitonga, Standard]

Former Deputy President and DCP party leader Rigathi Gachagua has vowed to fight back against goons allegedly disrupting his political rallies, saying his supporters will defend themselves if the police fail to protect them.

Speaking during the opening of DCP offices in Nakuru, Gachagua said they had received intelligence that the National Police Service (NPS) had been instructed to keep off areas where his rallies were being held.

Gachagua spoke a day after goons attacked his convoy at Kaptembwo in Nakuru West Sub-County, forcing him to abandon a DCP campaign rally and flee the scene alongside other leaders.

Six vehicles belonging to leaders, including Ol-Kalou MP Samuel Waweru, were vandalised during the incident as DCP leaders and supporters scrambled for safety.

Gachagua accused President William Ruto of allegedly planning the chaos through a Nakuru MP who, he claimed, had paid goons to disrupt his rallies.

“President William Ruto planned the chaos using a Nakuru MP who paid goons to attack us. This was despite his assurance that our campaign rallies would be protected,” Gachagua said.

He claimed he had received credible intelligence that police officers had been advised to keep away from Kaptembwo during the attack.

Gachagua further alleged that although the MP was associated with the Jubilee Party, he was being used by President Ruto to cause chaos.

“I have also spoken to Jubilee Party leaders to put their house in order. If it is proven that the MP is being used by the President, then he should be removed. That will inform how we relate to the Jubilee Party,” he said.

The former Deputy President said goons had allegedly been deployed to cause chaos at various stopovers, but some police officers who were unhappy with the Kenya Kwanza administration had provided his team with intelligence.

“We stood down our guard, hoping for protection from the government, but we are now on high alert and we will protect ourselves,” Gachagua said.

He also accused senior police officers in Nakuru of allegedly working with goons to disrupt his rallies.

According to Gachagua, junior police officers were unhappy with being allegedly forced to work with goons to cause chaos, steal property and kill Kenyans.

“These police officers have reduced salaries, they are not funded, they lack fuel and they are suffering,” he said.

World.title: Justice Department reaches $400 million settlement with TikTok over child privacy case
World.content:
New York —

TikTok and its parent company, ByteDance, reached a $400 million settlement with the US Justice Department over children’s privacy litigation on Friday, one of the largest amounts yet for a case of this kind.

The Justice Department first sued TikTok in 2024, claiming the app failed to stop children from joining the app and unlawfully collected their personal data. That violated the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), the Justice Department said.

It’s the latest settlement in an onslaught of lawsuits and scrutiny against major tech companies and social media platforms, alleging harm to children.

Friday’s settlement is “one of the largest recoveries ever obtained in a COPPA case,” a press release from the Justice Department said.

As part of the settlement, TikTok will immediately pay $300 million, and then another $100 million related to a 2019 Federal Trade Commission order involving Musical.ly, a video-sharing app Bytedance bought in 2017 and merged with TikTok.

The lawsuit in 2024 stemmed from that 2019 agreement. The Justice Department alleged that TikTok continued to collect data on children, such as email addresses, phone numbers and location data, and failed to comply with requests from parents to delete their children’s information, all in violation of the agreement, which required that the company take specific measures to abide by COPPA.

In 2024, TikTok said many of the allegations “relate to past events and practices that are factually inaccurate or have been addressed.”

Since the lawsuit, TikTok has implemented a number of changes, including “extensive measures designed to strengthen safeguards for younger users, improve age-related controls, and enhance parental oversight,” the Justice Department said in the press release.

Last year, TikTok announced it would spin off its American assets to mostly American investors, such as Oracle and private equity firm Silver Lake, a deal pushed by President Donald Trump.

CNN has reached out to TikTok for comment. There has been no determination of liability in the claims.

World.title: Strait of Hormuz traffic this week was 20% of pre-war average, though US says “oil is flowing”
World.content:
The number of ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz rose 27 percent in the past week, according to a CNN analysis of figures from the UK Maritime Trade Operations center (UKMTO), which recorded 103 entering and 89 leaving.

However, that is only 20 percent of the seven-day pre-war average, with the waterway still a focal point of the Iran war.

Most vessels were flagged from Panama (7) and Liberia (6), with none from the United States. The most common type of vessel traveling through the strait was the product tanker, which typically transports refined petroleum products.

For now, the evidence shows the US Navy gaining ground in the strait while Iran loses much of its control, with more than 80 percent of liquids transiting over the past two weeks taking the Omani route – a UN-authorized shipping channel that Iran vehemently opposes.

Earlier this week, the US Navy helped ship more than 15 million barrels of oil and products out of the strait and another five million via pipelines, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Saturday on X.

World.title: Iran: Trump’s economic threat paves the way for “return to full-scale classic colonialism”
World.content:
Iran pushed back on US President Donald Trump’s threat of an “economic D-Day,” calling it “a recipe for an abysmal return to full-scale classic colonialism.”

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said on Friday the United States’ declaration of new economic sanctions against the country is an “assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty over every independent Member State of the United Nations.”

The US president had earlier threatened “the MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION” against Iran in a social media post on August 19.

He also warned there would be economic consequences for countries that continue to do business with Tehran.

“Economic coercion designed to force a sovereign State to alter its lawful policy choices constitutes an outright internationally wrongful act,” Baghaei added in Friday’s post on X. “Compliance purchases no immunity or respect; it merely concedes that one’s banks, enterprises, and airports operate only under a foreign licence.”

The Iranian Foreign Ministry warned that those who order or implement the levies “are liable to prosecution and punishment,” reported state media IRIB.

World.title: North Korea boosts support for Russia to include drone operators, Ukraine says
World.content:
Kyiv —

A new wave of North Korean troops, already numbering 8,500 in Russia, contains a drone unit that could attack targets inside Ukraine, according to a senior Ukrainian intelligence official.

North Korea, who signed a NATO-style mutual defense pact with Russia two years ago, has been sending troops to assist Moscow’s military operations since late 2024 and may be asked to contribute up to 50,000 more when President Vladimir Putin meets his counterpart Kim Jong Un in September, according to Major General Vadym Skibitskiy, Deputy Head of Ukrainian Defense Intelligence.

Such a move would mark a significant expansion of Moscow and Pyongyang’s military cooperation and comes as Ukraine is running painfully short of air defenses. It is another sign that Russia’s resources are stretched thin and welcoming to assistance, despite public statements of their economic resilience and military-industrial capacity.

Skibitskiy said the North Korean troops already deployed are spread mostly in Russia’s Kursk region and include a thousand engineers and deminers. They also comprise 400 drone operators, many of whom have gained experience either in or from previous North Korean deployments, and whose drones will likely be used to both survey and attack targets inside Ukraine.

North Korea’s deepening ties with Russia are troubling many in the NATO alliance, particularly after President Donald Trump announced on Sunday that military drills with South Korea would be scaled down so as not to antagonize Kim Jong Un – the reclusive North Korean leader whom Trump is eager to meet with again.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un pictured speaking during the opening ceremony of a memorial honoring North Korean troops killed while fighting for Russia in the war against Ukraine. KCNA/Reuters

Kim’s powerful sister, Kim Yo Jong, denied claims that tens of thousands more North Koreans would soon join Russia’s efforts, calling it a “groundless self-fabricated scenario.”

Ukrainian intelligence suggests North Korean troops sent to Russia will not fight on Ukrainian territory, Skibitskiy said, but will reinforce Russia’s rear positions, freeing up Russian troops for assaults inside Ukraine.

Although Ukraine first warned that North Korean troops were using attack drones on their territory last October, this is the first indication the new wave of troops will have this capability. On top of Putin’s likely request for more troops, some 25,000 North Koreans have so far been deployed or rotated through Russia’s military, Skibitskiy added.

The first North Korean deployment began in the Kursk region in October 2024, to repel a Ukrainian incursion, the first on Russian soil since the Nazis. North Korea remained silent for months about its initial deployment of troops to help Russia’s war machine, only confirming its soldiers were fighting against Ukraine in April 2025. An estimated 10,000 North Koreans were deployed and suffered significant casualties, having used suicidal tactics to rush Ukrainian positions en masse.

North Korea’s willingness to sustain such losses reflects the reach of Russia’s global alliances and Moscow’s need for extra manpower. The wounded returned to North Korea able to teach their colleagues about drone warfare and the new reality of the tech-dominated frontlines.

Highlighting the strength of the two countries’ ties, Russian state media has shown images of North Korean troops in training inside Russia over the past year, and Kim Jong Un opened a memorial to North Korea’s Ukraine dead in April.

Skibitskiy also highlighted the extent to which North Korea is helping with missile technology for Russia’s offensive.

He said that before August last year, at least 150 KN 23 or KN 24 ballistic missiles had been sent by North Korea for use inside Ukraine, and another 120 were promised. Such weapons are proving increasingly difficult for Kyiv to shoot down, with supplies of US Patriot interceptors – one of the few systems capable of taking down ballistic missiles pretty much exhausted.

A representative from the prosecutor’s office shows parts of an unidentified missile, on January 6, 2024, which Ukrainian authorities believe to be made in North Korea and was used in a Russian strike on Kharkiv. Vyacheslav Madiyevskyy/Reuters

Forty of those have been delivered, Skibitskiy said, and two are suspected to have been used in Radushne, in the Dnipro Region, on 30 July in an attack that killed at least four children from the same family.

About 90 personnel have been sent to Voronzeh to assist with missile launches, he said, with ten large cargo flights, possibly containing missiles from North Korea, landing in the Baltimore aerodrome in Voronezh area.

Skibitskiy said more modern versions of the missiles had an extended range of 800km, but often landed 15-19km off target. He said North Korea was using the launches into Ukraine to improve their targeting and payload.

In return for supplying Russia with manpower and munitions, North Korea has asked for the Russian S400 air defence system and has already received a Pantsir 1 surface to air missile launcher, Skibitskiy said

World.title: PM: Tanzania’s Julius Nyerere Dam project showcases Egypt’s growing soft power in Africa
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said Friday that the giant Julius Nyerere Dam and Hydroelectric Power Station in Tanzania, implemented by an Egyptian consortium, stands as a prominent example of Egypt’s soft power in Africa.

Speaking exclusively to Extra News, Madbouly said it was an honor to attend the inauguration and commencement of operations at the dam and power station on behalf of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.

Madbouly said the project’s successful completion was the result of close and continuous follow-up by President Sisi throughout its various implementation stages.

He noted that the government had submitted monthly reports to the president detailing progress on the project, underscoring the importance the Egyptian state attached to its completion.

He added that the leaderships of Egypt and Tanzania had maintained close coordination and issued continuous directives to overcome obstacles and facilitate the project’s implementation.

The inauguration marks a major milestone in Egyptian-Tanzanian cooperation, with the project having been carried out by an Egyptian consortium comprising The Arab Contractors and Elsewedy Electric, under the supervision and oversight of the Egyptian government.

The Julius Nyerere project is one of Tanzania’s major strategic undertakings in the field of hydroelectric power generation. Built on the Rufiji River, the project is designed to help meet the country’s growing electricity needs and strengthen its power-generation capacity.

The project is also expected to contribute to reducing flood risks and supporting Tanzania’s economic development plans.

The landmark project reflects the growing scope of Egyptian-Tanzanian cooperation in infrastructure and energy, particularly through large-scale projects aimed at supporting sustainable development and improving essential services.

The prime minister said the Julius Nyerere Dam project stands as a testament to Egyptian expertise in implementing major international projects, highlighting it as clear evidence of the strong partnership between Egypt’s public sector and private companies.

In exclusive remarks to Extra News, Madbouly said the project also refutes previous claims that Egypt opposes development in Nile Basin countries.

He stressed that Egypt has always supported development efforts in the Nile Basin in a way that serves the interests of Egypt and Sudan.

“The Nile water issue is a matter of existential importance to Egypt,” Madbouly stressed.

Earlier Friday, Madbouly departed Cairo International Airport for Dodoma, the capital of Tanzania, heading a high-level delegation to attend, on behalf of President Abdel Fattah El Sisi, the inauguration of the Julius Nyerere Dam and Hydroelectric Power Station.

The landmark project was implemented by the Egyptian consortium of the Arab Contractors and Elsewedy Electric.

Madbouly said his participation, on behalf of President Sisi, in the inauguration ceremony, attended by Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan, reflects Egypt’s commitment to strengthening intra-African cooperation and building successful strategic partnerships with countries across the continent.

He said these partnerships seek to advance sustainable development through joint projects in a range of sectors, contributing to greater progress and prosperity for peoples in Africa.

World.title: Egypt economy shows resilience against shocks: planning minister
World.content:
Minister of Planning and Economic Development Ahmed Rostom affirmed that the Egyptian economy has demonstrated clear resilience against regional and global geopolitical shocks, noting that performance indicators reflect established stability, with growth reaching five percent in Q3 of the last fiscal year and 5.2 percent over the first nine months.

This came during his meeting with Forbes Global Properties CEO Michael Gilbert and Magnom Properties CEO Maged Marei to discuss expanding Egyptian market investments and the real estate sector’s role in advancing Vision 2030 sustainable development goals.

He pointed out that the construction, building, and real estate investment sector has become a primary growth driver, serving as a strategic engine propelling dozens of feeding industries and ranking among top employment generators.

The minister concluded the meeting by affirming the government’s commitment to supporting investment entities and activating the State Ownership Policy Document to grant the private sector greater space to lead development and improve citizens’ living standards.

World.title: Damietta Port handles 30 vessels, thousands of tons of cargo in 24 hours
World.content:
Damietta Port received 15 general cargo and container ships over the past 24 hours, while 15 vessels departed, bringing the total number of ships undergoing loading and unloading operations to 24, and total handled vessels to 30.

Damietta Port Authority media center said in a statement on Friday that general cargo exports reached 13,444 tons, comprising 4,500 tons of beet feed, 1,000 tons of urea, 5,000 tons of bagged gypsum, 162 tons of clinker, 250 tons of molasses, and 2,532 tons of miscellaneous goods.

General cargo imports totaled 26,190 tons, including 6,489 tons of scrap metal, 864 tons of beech wood, 922 tons of plywood, 15,415 tons of corn, and 2,500 tons of diverse goods, while container traffic recorded 1,002 TEUs exported, 323 TEUs imported, and 2,419 transit TEUs.

The public sector grain silo at the port held 36,582 tons of wheat, while private sector stores held 27,390 tons, with total truck movement logging 4,699 trips.

The statement added that the Ro-Ro vessel “GALLIPOLI SEAWAYS”, operating between Damietta and Italy’s Trieste, departed on Friday after handling 4,411 tons of vegetables, fruits, aluminum cables, textiles, car wiring harnesses, LED switches, connectors, and private cars bound for several European countries and Morocco.

World.title: 8 nations condemn Israeli settlement expansion and E1 project
World.content:
Foreign ministers of Egypt, Qatar, Jordan, the UAE, Indonesia, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia voiced their categorical condemnation of Israel’s ongoing illegal settlement policies in the occupied Palestinian territory, rejecting the E1 settlement plan and related activities east of occupied East Jerusalem.

In a joint statement on Friday, the ministers renewed their condemnation of settler violence and violations against Palestinians and their property, backed by Israeli occupation authorities.

They emphasized that such actions do not diminish the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people, constitute breaches of international law and relevant UN resolutions, and pose a severe threat to regional and global peace.

The ministers warned that the E1 plan is a dangerous escalation advancing settlement expansion and annexation, severing the territorial contiguity of the West Bank and East Jerusalem, and threatening the viability of an independent Palestinian state along 1967 lines.

They stressed that these measures directly defy international peace efforts, notably President Donald Trump’s comprehensive peace plan, which rejects annexation and forced displacement, and contradict Trump’s commitment against West Bank annexation to resolve the conflict.

Reaffirming the two-state solution based on international law and UN resolutions, the ministers called it the only viable path to a just, lasting, and comprehensive peace.

They warned that moves undermining the two-state solution will escalate tensions and jeopardize regional and international stability.

The ministers backed all accountability measures, including international sanctions against individuals and entities responsible for illegal settlement activities and annexation policies, urging an immediate halt to all funding supporting settlement establishment or expansion.

They stressed that the lack of accountability perpetuates violations and damages prospects for a comprehensive peace.

The ministers called for immediate action to halt the E1 scheme, reverse associated measures, and end all actions altering the demographic and geographical character of occupied Palestinian land.

They urged the UN Security Council and international community to fulfill their legal obligations by halting settlement expansion, protecting the Palestinian people, and upholding their right to self-determination and statehood.

World.title: Liberia: LNP Denies Starlink Use, Clarifies Vehicle Procurement Amid Public Questions
World.content:
MONROVIA — The Liberia National Police (LNP) has clarified questions surrounding the institution’s internet connectivity and procurement of operational vehicles, rejecting claims that its facilities use Starlink internet services and distancing its vehicle purchases and internet arrangements from individuals linked to Liberia’s ongoing narcotics investigation.

In a statement issued Friday, August 21, the police said its internet services are provided through the Liberia Telecommunications Corporation (LIBTELCO/LTC Mobile) under an official institutional contract.

The clarification comes amid public inquiries and discussions concerning the resources being used by the country’s principal law enforcement institution, particularly as authorities continue a high-profile investigation into alleged narcotics trafficking.

The LNP stated that it does not use Starlink internet service at any of its facilities. “The LNP does not use Starlink internet service at any of its facilities,” the institution said, explaining that its internet connectivity is instead provided by LIBTELCO/LTC Mobile through an official agreement.

The police also addressed questions concerning its operational vehicles, confirming that it procured used vehicles from Guardian Fleet, a company based in the United States.

According to the LNP, the vehicles were acquired to strengthen the police institution’s operational capacity, particularly in the areas of mobility, patrols and emergency response.

The police said the procurement forms part of efforts to enhance its ability to respond to security needs across Liberia.

The clarification is particularly significant because public discussions surrounding the LNP’s resources have emerged against the backdrop of an ongoing investigation into an alleged narcotics trafficking network.

The LNP, however, said its official institutional records do not substantiate claims linking either the vehicle procurement or its internet services to individuals associated with the narcotics investigation.

“Official institutional records do not support claims connecting these services or vehicle procurements to individuals associated with the ongoing narcotics investigation,” the police said.

The statement did not identify the specific individuals or claims prompting the clarification, but the institution appeared to be responding directly to questions circulating publicly regarding its procurement arrangements and the source of its internet connectivity.

The police emphasized that its clarification was intended to provide the public with accurate information about the institution’s operational arrangements.

The LNP also reaffirmed its commitment to transparency and accountability, acknowledging the public’s right to seek information about the activities and resources of a national security institution.

According to the police, members of the public are entitled to ask questions about institutional expenditures, procurement decisions and operational resources. At the same time, however, the LNP urged caution in public commentary concerning matters connected to ongoing investigations.

The institution called for responsible public discussion, stressing the importance of protecting the integrity of active investigations as well as the rights of individuals involved. “The LNP respects the public’s right to seek information and remains committed to transparency and accountability,” the statement said.

The police further urged responsible public commentary that protects both the integrity of ongoing investigations and the rights of all persons concerned.

The clarification comes as the LNP and other security institutions remain under intense public scrutiny over their handling of the country’s narcotics investigation.

The investigation has generated widespread public interest, with questions being raised about the movement of suspected narcotics, individuals allegedly connected to the case and the actions of various institutions involved in the government’s response.

Against that backdrop, the LNP’s decision to publicly clarify its internet and vehicle arrangements signals an effort to distinguish its established institutional procurement and service arrangements from allegations or speculation surrounding the narcotics investigation.

The police’s reference to official institutional records suggests that it considers its procurement documentation and contractual arrangements the appropriate basis for determining whether any connection exists between its resources and individuals under investigation.

The LNP’s latest statement therefore seeks to establish a distinction between legitimate public inquiries and claims that the institution says are not supported by its official records.

World.title: Liberia: Bong Native Flomo Calls on Justice Ministry to Release Jewel Howard-Taylor to Her Lawyers
World.content:
MONROVIA — Bong County native residing in the United States, David Flomo, has called on the Ministry of Justice to release former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor into the custody of her lawyers, arguing that the government can continue its investigation into the alleged drug case while ensuring that the former vice president receives proper legal and medical attention.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

Flomo made the appeal in a Facebook post amid heightened public attention surrounding Howard-Taylor’s detention and subsequent charging in connection with the government’s ongoing investigation into alleged narcotics trafficking.

“While the fight against drugs in Liberia will have no boundaries and special protections for all citizens, however, the former vice President must be treated with respect and dignity,” Flomo wrote.

He specifically urged the government to release Howard-Taylor to her lawyer and consider placing her under house arrest after she leaves the hospital.

Flomo’s call follows Howard-Taylor’s detention after she was prevented Wednesday by joint security authorities from traveling out of Liberia. The former vice president was subsequently invited by the joint security for questioning as investigators expanded their probe into the alleged drug trafficking network.

Following her appearance before investigators, Howard-Taylor was charged in connection with the ongoing investigation, bringing the former national leader directly into a case that has attracted significant public and political attention.

Howard-Taylor, a native of Sanoyea District in Bong County, has since experienced health complications while in detention and was taken for medical treatment after reportedly falling sick.

Her health condition has become an additional concern surrounding the former vice president’s detention, particularly as authorities and her legal representatives face the next stage of the proceedings.

It is against this backdrop that Flomo is asking the Ministry of Justice to reconsider the conditions under which Howard-Taylor is being held. According to Flomo, releasing her to her lawyers would not prevent the government from continuing its investigation or pursuing the charges against her. Rather, he believes such an arrangement would allow authorities to maintain the legal process while ensuring that the former vice president receives appropriate care and representation.

Flomo also questioned whether Howard-Taylor should be considered a flight risk, arguing that her status as a former senior government official means she continues to benefit from government security protection.

“She isn’t flight risk because she protected for life by government security,” he stated.

His recommendation for house arrest therefore appears to be based on the belief that authorities can maintain sufficient oversight of Howard-Taylor without keeping her in conventional detention, particularly while she is recovering from her reported illness.

The appeal comes as the government continues to defend its broader campaign against illicit drugs and its decision to investigate individuals allegedly connected to the narcotics trade, regardless of their political or social standing.

LiThe former vice president’s case has attracted heightened attention because of her previous position as Liberia’s second-highest constitutional official and her long history in national politics. Before serving as vice president, Howard-Taylor represented Bong County in the Liberian Senate.

World.title: Liberia: Golden Touch Pushes Back Against MPR/APM Investigation, Says Dukuly’s Role Was Lawful
World.content:
Golden Touch said that description was inaccurate and insisted that Dukuly’s involvement with the company was neither improper nor unlawful. “There is nothing improper, unlawful, or fraudulent about Mr. Dukuly’s involvement with Golden Touch,” the company said.

MONROVIA — Golden Touch Health Care LLC has mounted a strong defense of its operations and the involvement of Sekou Dukuly, rejecting what it describes as inaccurate implications contained in an investigation published by MPR News and APM Reports.

The healthcare company issued its response Friday, four days after the August 17 publication, maintaining that it has operated with a commitment to providing stable and long-term care to Minnesotans with significant medical and behavioral health needs.

Golden Touch said the report prompted the company to clarify its position, particularly concerning claims surrounding Dukuly and his relationship with the healthcare organization.

At the center of the company’s response is its rejection of the characterization that Dukuly was “moonlighting” in Minnesota while simultaneously living and working in public service in Liberia.

Golden Touch said that description was inaccurate and insisted that Dukuly’s involvement with the company was neither improper nor unlawful.

“There is nothing improper, unlawful, or fraudulent about Mr. Dukuly’s involvement with Golden Touch,” the company said.

The company did not disclose additional details about Dukuly’s specific responsibilities in its statement but maintained that his involvement with Golden Touch should not be interpreted as evidence of wrongdoing.

Golden Touch also defended the structure of its Minnesota operations, emphasizing that it works to comply with applicable assisted living laws and regulations.

According to the company, licensed assisted living directors are present in Minnesota to oversee the care and supervision provided to residents at its facilities.

The company said those arrangements are intended to ensure that residents receive the necessary care and oversight required under Minnesota regulations.

Golden Touch further highlighted its history in the healthcare sector, saying it has provided services since 2017 to residents with complex medical and behavioral health needs.

The company said its work has helped some residents progress toward greater independence, while its directors, caregivers and nurses have remained responsible for providing services throughout the year.

“Our directors, caregivers, and nurses show up 365 days a year,” Golden Touch said, adding that it stands behind their professionalism and compassion.

Alongside its defense of its operations, Golden Touch expressed sympathy to families who lost loved ones while receiving care from the company.

The statement said the company recognizes the significance of those losses and extended condolences to affected families before addressing the issues raised by the MPR/APM investigation.

Golden Touch’s response also took issue with what it described as political implications arising from the report.

The company suggested that some individuals could attempt to use the report for political purposes, but it maintained that such considerations would not change its focus on healthcare delivery.

“It is unfortunate that some may seek political gain based on the inaccurate implications made in the MPR/APM report,” the company stated.

Rather than engage in what it considers political distractions, Golden Touch said it intends to continue concentrating on its healthcare responsibilities and the people who depend on its services.

The company’s statement places particular emphasis on its commitment to Minnesota residents, arguing that its primary responsibility remains providing quality care to people with medical and behavioral health needs.

The dispute highlights the broader importance of oversight, management and compliance within residential healthcare facilities, particularly those serving residents requiring specialized support.

Golden Touch said its continued operations are guided by Minnesota’s assisted living requirements and that licensed professionals oversee care at its facilities.

Golden Touch said it will remain focused on its stated mission rather than the controversy surrounding the report. “Golden Touch will remain focused on what it has always done: providing quality care to Minnesotans in need,” the company said.

World.title: Former Liberian Goalkeeper Melvin King Reportedly Dies in Côte d’Ivoire
World.content:
Monrovia — Former Liberian goalkeeper Melvin King has reportedly died in Côte d’Ivoire, according to reports coming from the country.
